subject: Lincoln Financial — dedicated pool saturation & reserved-capacity throughput shortfall
messages:

Cc: Procurement <procurement@lincolnfin.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 22:15:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency and 5xx — are we hitting our reserved capacity?

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing steady latency increases around 21:40 PDT and a growing 5xx rate across our production endpoints. Our dashboard shows a spike in token queues and a reserved throughput shortfall message. This is impacting our live risk-scoring flows.

Can you confirm whether Lincoln's dedicated GPU pool is saturated or if there's another root cause? We need ETA on mitigation — the streams are business-critical and our ops team is standing by.

I attached a short slice of our logs and a screenshot from our observability dashboard.

Thanks,
Sarah Nguyen
Director, Platform Operations
Lincoln Financial

Attachments: ops-logs-20270416.txt (text), dashboard-snap-2140.png (image)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 00:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 5xx — are we hitting our reserved capacity?

Hi Sarah — thanks for the alert and the logs.

Short answer: we do see the dedicated pool for your reservation at sustained utilization above the target headroom. There is also an unusual traffic pattern from a small cohort of tenants that increased batch sizes and pushed token concurrency beyond the planned profile, which is amplifying queueing.

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Throttled non-critical background jobs tied to your account (temporary).
- Opened a short-lived burst window on the dedicated pool (pending your approval for overage billing).
- Engaged infra to increase KV-cache TTL for common prefixes to reduce repeated decode work.

We need a 30-minute call to confirm burst authorization and share a timeline for reverting the burst once queues clear. Ben and Irene (cc'd) are with me — Ben will coordinate procurement language if you want us to draft it.

Irene: can you start a prioritized play for cache tweaks + kernel fallback for one model family? We should try to reduce per-token latency while burst is online.

Sarah — please confirm whether your team can approve a one-hour burst (we'll capture the usage and apply to the next invoice or bill via procurement). If procurement needs formal wording, Ben will follow up.

—Kimberly

Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 5xx — are we hitting our reserved capacity?

Hi Sarah — quick technical update and proposed short-term/medium-term actions.

Root cause (preliminary):
- A small set of clients started sending larger batched requests with longer sequences around 21:30 PDT. The model runtime selected kernels optimized for shorter sequences; that mismatch increased per-token CPU/GPU time under high concurrency and amplified queueing.
- Simultaneously, one of your heavy prompt prefixes had low cache hit rates due to previously low TTLs, so we were rebuilding KV caches more frequently than expected.

Short-term remediation (now -> 2 hours):
1) Approve 60-minute burst on dedicated capacity (we provision additional nodes and temporarily increase your headroom). Estimated cost: ~0.9 token-hours * 1,200 units = $1,080 (Ben to confirm exact).
2) Apply kernel fallback for the affected model family to the lower-latency path (reduces per-token time by ~12% in our tests).
3) Increase KV-cache TTL for the frequent prefixes (should cut repeated decode work by ~30%).

Medium-term (3-14 days):
- Work with your infra to pin model variants for production windows (smaller effective sequence length) and add a soft admission control on batch sizes during peak windows.
- Update the reserved throughput profile for the upcoming quarter to include a 15% surge buffer if your traffic pattern remains volatile.

We will monitor the queues; I'll post another update in 30 minutes after the burst is live.

--Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
